title: Per-channel compensation & autotune pipeline for activation-aware INT8 (SmoothComp)
creator: Liam Chen
description: Implement a per-channel activation compensation and autotune pipeline (internal name: SmoothComp) to generate INT8 profiles that minimize post-quantization accuracy loss while maintaining runtime throughput targets. This ticket covers the calibration harness changes, exportable profile format, runtime kernel hints for per-channel compensators, and a staged rollout plan with canary fallbacks to FP16/FP32 variants. Goals: (1) reduce cross-layer activation variance impact for Transformers with layernorm/GEGLU patterns, (2) produce compact profile artifacts compatible with Dedicated and Private deployments, and (3) provide an autotune job that recommends quant parameters per workload and SLO (latency/cost/accuracy).
acceptance_criteria: Calibration harness can produce per-channel scale/shift compensation vectors and serialize them to a profile JSON compatible with runtime profile schema
Runtime kernel accepts compensator hints and applies them without >10% p95 latency regression at target batch sizes
End-to-end eval on SQuAD/LLama-like workloads shows <=1.0% absolute F1 degradation compared to baseline FP16 for supported models (gpt-style and encoder-decoder)
Autotune job returns suggested quant config for a workload within 3 iterations on average and stores decisions in model metadata
Canary rollout procedure documented and validated; automatic fallback to model-variant if accuracy delta exceeds threshold during rollout
design_notes: We considered two approaches: (A) per-tensor activation rescale (low overhead, less accurate) and (B) per-channel compensators derived from activation statistics (higher accuracy, extra memory and compute). Chosen approach B with a sparse representation: store compensators only for layers with activation variance > threshold. Compensation will be implemented as a lightweight pointwise rescale before matmul kernels. Kernel changes will expose a compensator pointer in the next generation of fused matmul kernels. Trade-offs: extra memory for profiles (~0.5-2.0% model size), small compute on hot paths; mitigated by caching compensators in GPU L2 and applying only when sequence-length > X. Compatibility: runtime falls back to per-tensor path if kernel or device lacks compensator support.
implementation_plan: 1) Extend calibration harness to collect per-channel activation histograms and compute compensators (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/quant-harness/pull/182)
2) Define profile schema v1.3 (confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/SmoothComp+Profile+Schema) and update exporter
3) Implement compensator application in fused matmul kernels (runtime PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/599)
4) Add kernel selector heuristics to prefer compensator-enabled kernels when profile present
5) Build autotune driver that runs small calibration traces and simulates SLO trade-offs (job: optimize-quant/autotune-2025)
6) Add CI validation: accuracy regression tests and perf microbenchmarks across GPU types
7) Rollout: internal canary -> selected customers on Dedicated -> gradual Private deploys with opt-in
test_plan: Integration test: run autotune job and validate suggested profile on cifar-like synthetic traces
E2E accuracy sweep using eval harness (eval-service job id: eval-2025-03-05-23) comparing FP16 vs INT8+SmoothComp
Perf test: p95 latency and throughput at batch sizes 1, 8, 32 on A100 and T4; ensure <10% p95 regression
Backward compatibility check: ensure fallback flow yields identical outputs when compensators disabled
dependencies: Security review for profile artifacts (if contains model-identifying traces)
